text: 3 PREFACE At the dawn of the 19th century when nationalism was introduced to the Balkans and as new states began to form out of the ashes of the Ottoman Empire, dialectal languages were viewed as simplistic, backwards, limited and, to some degree, expressionless.
text_raw:
3
PREFACE
At the dawn of the 19th century when nationalism was introduced to the
Balkans and as new states began to form out of the ashes of the Ottoman
Empire, dialectal languages were viewed as simplistic, backwards, limited
and, to some degree, expressionless.

text: They were deemed vulgar and were scoffed at.
text_raw:
They were deemed vulgar and were
scoffed at.

text: Modern and literary languages were created to replace them and students were discouraged from speaking them because they were presented as the languages of uneducated peasants.
text_raw:
Modern and literary languages were created to replace them and
students were discouraged from speaking them because they were
presented as the languages of uneducated peasants.

text: Generations later, as the newly created societies began to culturally mature and search for their roots, attitudes towards dialectal languages began to change.
text_raw:
Generations later, as the newly created societies began to culturally
mature and search for their roots, attitudes towards dialectal languages
began to change.

text: Dialects began to be seen no longer as vulgar and limited but rather as the mothers of modern languages and the sources of modern cultures.
text_raw:
Dialects began to be seen no longer as vulgar and limited
but rather as the mothers of modern languages and the sources of modern
cultures.

text: Dialectal languages, at least in the Balkans, are the most natural and longest lasting cultural elements that not only defined the uniqueness of certain societies but also, in a positive way, highlight the diversities within them.
text_raw:
Dialectal languages, at least in the Balkans, are the most natural and
longest lasting cultural elements that not only defined the uniqueness of
certain societies but also, in a positive way, highlight the diversities within
them.

text: The Balkans has always been a multicultural, multiethnic region with various ethnicities living together.
text_raw:
The Balkans has always been a multicultural, multiethnic region
with various ethnicities living together.

text: Languages have been the predominant factors of cultural divide in a positive way.
text_raw:
Languages have been the
predominant factors of cultural divide in a positive way.

text: And within each culture, at least with the Macedonians, a number of micro-cultures existed predominantly defined by unique characteristics such as dress, colour, pattern, song, dance and obviously dialectal language.
text_raw:
And within each
culture, at least with the Macedonians, a number of micro-cultures existed
predominantly defined by unique characteristics such as dress, colour,
pattern, song, dance and obviously dialectal language.

text: Before the introduction of nationalism these cultural elements were seen as positive characteristics that uniquely identified each micro-culture in those societies.
text_raw:
Before the
introduction of nationalism these cultural elements were seen as positive
characteristics that uniquely identified each micro-culture in those
societies.

text: Macedonians, no matter from which corner of Macedonia, recognized a dress with certain colours and patterns as belonging to a certain region of Macedonia.
text_raw:
Macedonians, no matter from which corner of Macedonia, recognized
a dress with certain colours and patterns as belonging to a certain region of
Macedonia.

text: They all knew how to dance to the “Bufskoto”, “Tikveshkoto” or “Bitolskoto” Oro but also knew it belonged to the people of Buf, Tikvesh or Bitola.
text_raw:
They all knew how to dance to the “Bufskoto”, “Tikveshkoto”
or “Bitolskoto” Oro but also knew it belonged to the people of Buf,
Tikvesh or Bitola.

text: Their culture was based on long standing practical traditions but was by no means culturally limited, vulgar or unnatural.
text_raw:
Their culture was based on long standing practical
traditions but was by no means culturally limited, vulgar or unnatural.

text: In fact, as people are discovering today, it was the most natural course of cultural evolution that a society could experience.
text_raw:
In
fact, as people are discovering today, it was the most natural course of
cultural evolution that a society could experience.

text: What was truly unnatural was the attempt of our 19th century authorities to destroy it and replace it with something artificial for the sake of standardization and modernization.
text_raw:
What was truly
unnatural was the attempt of our 19th century authorities to destroy it and
replace it with something artificial for the sake of standardization and
modernization.

text: It is most unfortunate that Macedonians, who recognize that the strength of a culture is in its diversity, were not allowed to form their own state and thus were subjected to cultural destruction.
text_raw:
It is most unfortunate that Macedonians, who recognize that the
strength of a culture is in its diversity, were not allowed to form their own
state and thus were subjected to cultural destruction.

text: Macedonian culture was seen as a threat to Macedonia’s occupiers who, in their attempts to create a monolithic and to a large extent fictional replacement, were bent on its destruction.
text_raw:
Macedonian culture
was seen as a threat to Macedonia’s occupiers who, in their attempts to
create a monolithic and to a large extent fictional replacement, were bent
on its destruction.

text: Some states,like Greece went as far as banning the Macedonian culture by making the Macedonian language in all its dialectal
text_raw:

Macedonian culture by making the Macedonian language in all its dialectal

text: In view of the resurgence of Macedonians needing to rediscover their roots, the study of dialects has become interesting and of importance.

text: There is urgent need to do this because I believe, with time and by the application of literary languages through the educational system, dialects will disappear forever.

There is
urgent need to do this because I believe, with time and by the application
of literary languages through the educational system, dialects will
disappear forever.

text: I am one of the last generations to be born in Oshchima, Lerin-Kostur Region, in a society that until as recently as half a century ago spoke a dialect of the Macedonian language.
text_raw:
I am one of the last generations to be born in
Oshchima, Lerin-Kostur Region, in a society that until as recently as half a
century ago spoke a dialect of the Macedonian language.

text: I still remember the language as it was spoken by the elders of Oshchima.
text_raw:
I still remember
the language as it was spoken by the elders of Oshchima.

text: Today, Oshchima is virtually extinct and it is a matter of time before this language too will cease to exist.
text_raw:
Today, Oshchima is virtually extinct and it is a matter of time before
this language too will cease to exist.

text: Oshchima is a small village located half way between Lerin and Kostur in Western Macedonia, now Greek occupied Macedonia, which in 1939, at its h eight, had about six-hundred residents.
text_raw:
Oshchima is a small village located
half way between Lerin and Kostur in Western Macedonia, now Greek
occupied Macedonia, which in 1939, at its h eight, had about six-hundred
residents.

text: By 1969 its population had dropped to less than a dozen people.
text_raw: By 1969 its population had dropped to less than a dozen people.

text: Now only a couple of families live there and all the younger generations speak Greek.
text_raw:
Now only a couple of families live there and all the younger generations
speak Greek.

text: Oshchima was hard hit and nearly destroyed by the Greek Civil War and most of its residents fled for Canada, Australia, the USA and the Republic of Macedonia.
text_raw:
Oshchima was hard hit and nearly destroyed by the Greek
Civil War and most of its residents fled for Canada, Australia, the USA
and the Republic of Macedonia.

text: Since the vast majority of new generations and future generations of Oshchimians live and will continue to live in English speaking countries, this book is my gift to them, to remind them of how their ancestors once spoke.
text_raw:
Since the vast majority of new generations and future generations of
Oshchimians live and will continue to live in English speaking countries,
this book is my gift to them, to remind them of how their ancestors once
spoke.

text: The publishing of this book was timed to coincide with the 100th anniversary of the organization “Benefit Society Oshchima” founded in 1907 by Oshchimian emigrants in Canada.
text_raw:
The publishing of this book was timed to coincide with the 100th
anniversary of the organization “Benefit Society Oshchima” founded in
1907 by Oshchimian emigrants in Canada.

text: This organization was founded to help newly landed Oshchimian emigrants adjust in the world.
text_raw:
This organization was founded
to help newly landed Oshchimian emigrants adjust in the world.

text: Over the years Benefit Society Oshchima evolved into an organization of unity and Macedonian culture bringing Oshchimians together and giving them a sense of belonging.

text: I would like to thank my parents Nikola and Sofia for their contribution to this book and for their help in clarifying the meaning of the more difficult words.

text: In putting this dictionary together, my attempt is to bring you a unique version of the Macedonian language as spoken by Oshchimians.
text_raw:
In putting this dictionary together, my attempt is to bring you a unique

text: The sixteen hundred or so words documented here are uniquely Oshchimian as they were spoken by the last generations living in Oshchima.
text_raw:
The
sixteen hundred or so words documented here are uniquely Oshchimian as
they were spoken by the last generations living in Oshchima.

text: I would like to remind the reader that this particular language, like all Macedonian dialects in Greece, was banned in the 1930’s by the Greek authorities and was made illegal to speak.
text_raw:
I would like
to remind the reader that this particular language, like all Macedonian
dialects in Greece, was banned in the 1930’s by the Greek authorities and

text: It is a miracle it has survived for this long.
text_raw: It is a miracle it has survived for this long.

text: 5 Introduction The dialectal Macedonian language presented here is a naturally evolving oral language that has been in use uncodified for many centuries.
text_raw:
5
Introduction
The dialectal Macedonian language presented here is a naturally
evolving oral language that has been in use uncodified for many centuries.

text: I have made every effort to present it in its exact form as it was spoken by generations before me and without grammatical adjustments or corrections.
text_raw:
I have made every effort to present it in its exact form as it was spoken by
generations before me and without grammatical adjustments or
corrections.

text: Like most natural languages, it follows logical patterns but not without some exceptions.
text_raw:
Like most natural languages, it follows logical patterns but not
without some exceptions.

text: My intent here was to document words and phrases as I remember them spoken and to not necessarily explain them grammatically.
text_raw:
My intent here was to document words and phrases as I remember
them spoken and to not necessarily explain them grammatically.

text: For grammatical clarifications, the reader is advised to consult the Macedonian literary language.
text_raw:
For
grammatical clarifications, the reader is advised to consult the Macedonian
literary language.
